rationale:
The copy gate's repair call has a max_tokens ceiling of 2000, set deliberately by migration 517 on 2026-08-21 with the rationale 'the answer is a handful of replacement sentences, and a section-sized ceiling would only buy room for the model to write an essay this gate would then reject'. That premise is now falsified by measurement, and 517 itself wrote down the failure mode it was accepting and the loud signal it would produce. This migration is what that signal was for.

MEASURED 2026-08-23 ~12:35Z over the live copy_gate* markers (a rolling window; orchestration_states is reaped and the population moved 42->44 during the measurement): the outcome separates perfectly on target count, with no exceptions either side. Markers with 1,2,3,5 targets (43 of them) ALL returned status=repaired. Markers with 9 and 10 targets (2) BOTH returned status=repair_unavailable and repaired nothing. That is not intermittent truncation, it is a hard capacity limit between 5 and 8 targets. Both failures carry the ceiling in their own error text: 'response truncated: stop_reason=max_tokens (output_tokens=2000 reached the configured cap, 2066 chars recovered)' at 10 targets, and the same with '0 chars recovered' at 9.

The cost is disproportionate because the failure is TOTAL rather than partial: the round is discarded whole, so a page with 10 constructions gets ZERO repaired while a page with 1 gets its one. Those 2 markers hold 19 of the 78 targets in the window - 24.4% of all repair targets are lost to the ceiling. For scale, the accounting hole fixed in 6e9cb411d (council f3046f0c, approved today) accounted for 12. The gate fails hardest on exactly the pages it exists for.

WHY 2000 CANNOT HOLD, and it is not about essays. (a) max_tokens is an enforced per-response ceiling THE MODEL IS NOT AWARE OF - it cannot pace itself to fit, it is simply cut, so a ceiling that is too small does not buy brevity, it buys nothing. (b) The answer is O(targets), not O(1): the model echoes both `from` and `to` per target, so a dense page's answer is several times a sparse page's. '' A handful of replacement sentences'' is the 1-target case, which is 36 of 44 markers, and is why this held for two days. (c) claude-sonnet-5 with no `thinking` block set runs ADAPTIVE THINKING, and thinking tokens draw on this same ceiling - that is 517's own stated warning, and the 9-target run recovering 0 characters of text is what it looks like.

WHY 16000 SPECIFICALLY: it is what the sibling step in the SAME sub-workflow already uses. generate_content, which writes an entire section, is at 16000, while the step that rewrites a few of its sentences was at 2000 - 8x smaller. 16000 is also the documented default ceiling for a non-streaming request. This preserves 517's instinct that the repair should not exceed the writer; it stops it being an order of magnitude below it.

COST: output tokens are billed as generated, not as reserved - the ceiling is a safety limit, not an allocation. The 36 one-target markers emit what they emit today and cost what they cost today. Only the dense pages, which currently produce nothing at all, spend more.

SCOPE, pre-empting the 'one call site of a class' objection that this lane's previous round raised: I ran the census rather than asserting it. Across EVERY anthropic call in the fleet over the last 3 days (llm_call_log, output_tokens >= max_tokens, the estate's own documented cut detector), exactly one step is hitting its output ceiling - this one, at 4 of 34 calls (11.8%). No other agent_type/step_name pair in the fleet has a single truncated call. This is not one instance of a widespread pattern; it is the only case.

WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT FIX: the ceiling is still fixed while plan.targets is unbounded (the page budget is a TOLERANCE, not a cap - every hit past it becomes a target). 16000 covers every page observed with a wide margin, and a dense enough page would truncate again - and would again fail loudly as repair_unavailable rather than silently. Chunking the targets across calls is the structural answer and is a CODE change; it is recorded in bugs_open/305 §27 rather than smuggled into a config migration.

plan.summary: Raise the copy gate's repair ceiling (rewrite_negations ai_service.max_tokens) from 2000 to 16000, anchored on the sibling generate_content step in the same sub-workflow. Config-only migration, live on apply, needle-gated on the current value so a re-run is a no-op and it cannot overwrite a later deliberate retune.

edits.rationale: One number. Needle-gated on max_tokens='2000' in the WHERE clause so a re-run is a 0-row no-op and a later deliberate retune by another session cannot be silently clobbered. Takes a snapshot_agent first, matching 517's pattern for this same row.
edits.sketch: UPDATE agent_definitions SET default_config = jsonb_set(default_config, '{workflow,steps,process_sections_loop,config,sub_workflow,steps,rewrite_negations,config,ai_service,max_tokens}', '16000'::jsonb), updated_at = now() WHERE type='page-content-writer' AND is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL AND default_config #>> '{...,rewrite_negations,action}' = 'rewrite_negations' AND default_config #>> '{...,ai_service,max_tokens}' = '2000';

edits.rationale: A verify block of bare SELECTs cannot stop a COMMIT (ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result), so the checks are DO/RAISE. Three of them: the new value is present exactly once; ai_service.model is still claude-sonnet-5 (a jsonb_set against a MOVED path mints an orphan key rather than failing, so the neighbour is asserted rather than assumed); and a RAISE WARNING, not an exception, if the generate_content anchor is no longer 16000 - that is a signal to re-read the rationale, not a reason to refuse the change. INDUCED before applying: run with the UPDATE skipped and it raises '569 FAILED: ... got 0', exit code 3.
edits.sketch: DO $$ ... IF n <> 1 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '569 FAILED: expected exactly 1 ... got %', n; END IF; IF model IS DISTINCT FROM 'claude-sonnet-5' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '569 FAILED: ai_service.model is % - the block moved'; END IF; IF mt IS DISTINCT FROM '16000' THEN RAISE WARNING '569 NOTE: generate_content max_tokens is % - the anchor moved'; END IF; $$;

edits.rationale: Needle-gated on 16000 so it cannot clobber a later retune. Its banner states what reverting re-arms - a measured, TOTAL failure on dense pages - and names the two circumstances in which reverting is nonetheless legitimate (spend, or a model change), each with the instruction to re-measure rather than return to a number that predates any measurement.
edits.sketch: UPDATE ... SET ... '2000'::jsonb ... WHERE ... max_tokens = '16000'; DO $$ ... RAISE EXCEPTION '569 ROLLBACK FAILED ...' ... $$;

grounded_in: 517_rewrite_negations_declares_its_own_ai_service.sql, the value being changed and its stated reasoning: 'max_tokens 2000 is deliberate and small: the answer is a handful of replacement sentences, and a section-sized ceiling would only buy room for the model to write an essay this gate would then reject.'

517, the failure mode it wrote down in advance and which has now occurred: 'If a future model runs adaptive thinking out of this budget the call yields no text, the repair fails CLOSED (splices nothing) and says repair_unavailable - loud, not silent, which is the whole reason that status exists.'
Live marker census 2026-08-23 ~12:35Z, targets vs outcome with no exceptions: 1 target/36 markers repaired; 2/2 repaired; 3/3 repaired; 5/2 repaired; 9/1 repair_unavailable; 10/1 repair_unavailable.

The two failures' own error text, carrying the applied ceiling: 'response truncated: stop_reason=max_tokens (output_tokens=2000 reached the configured cap, 2066 chars recovered)' and '... (output_tokens=2000 reached the configured cap, 0 chars recovered)'.

Fleet census over llm_call_log, 3 days, provider=anthropic, using the estate's documented cut detector (output_tokens >= max_tokens): exactly one step in the entire fleet is hitting its ceiling - process_sections_loop_iter_1_rewrite_negations, 4 of 34 calls, 11.8%. No other agent_type/step_name pair has a single truncated call.
The live sibling config in the same sub-workflow: generate_content ai_service.max_tokens = 16000 against rewrite_negations at 2000 - read from the live agent_definitions row, not from a seed.
CLAUDE.md's own durable rule, which is the detector used above: 'output_tokens == max_tokens means the completion was CUT, not finished.'
plan.risks:
SPEND is the real one, and it is bounded by how billing works rather than by the ceiling: output tokens are billed as generated, not reserved, so the 36 one-target markers (82% of traffic) cost exactly what they cost today. The delta is confined to dense pages, which currently spend their 2000 and produce nothing usable. A pathological run could now emit up to 16000 tokens of rewrites that AcceptNegationRewrite and the banned-claims scan then reject - wasted spend on one call, not a correctness problem, and the same structural rejection applies at 2000.

UNBOUNDED TARGETS, stated rather than fixed: the page budget is a tolerance, not a cap, so plan.targets has no upper bound and any fixed ceiling can eventually be exceeded. 16000 is 8x the current ceiling against a worst observed case of 10 targets, so the margin is wide, but the failure mode is unchanged in kind - it would truncate and say repair_unavailable. Chunking is the structural fix and is a code change; recorded as bugs_open/305 §27, not attempted here.

GO-SIDE DEFAULT UNCHANGED: rewrite_negations_action.go still falls back to options['max_tokens']=2000 when no ai_service config resolves. That path is currently unreachable for this step because 517 declares the config, and changing it is a code change requiring a roll; the config is the live control and is what this migration moves. Flagged so a reader does not conclude from the Go source that the ceiling is still 2000.

NOT A FIX FOR THE ACCOUNTING HOLE: a repair_unavailable marker still accounts for none of its targets, because the five early returns in runNegationRepair all precede the unansweredTargetRejections call at line 665. That is separate from 6e9cb411d and is documented in §27; this migration reduces how OFTEN that path is taken, it does not close it.
